_about: A6: contraindicated procedures. A row holds an answer only when it is signed: signoff true, reviewed_by, review_date, and at least one source. Signing is the owner's act (docs/authoring/SIGNING.md). Design and rulings: docs/A6_CONTRAINDICATED_PROCEDURES_DESIGN.md. P4 (oral intake with depressed consciousness) stays as A4's code until it has a source.

rows.hold_text: The answer advised a lumbar puncture, but raised or suspected raised ICP is recorded. A lumbar puncture is a recognised contraindication here. Use local protocol and medical control.
rows.extraction_notes: No corpus passage found for the LP contraindication (#98). The ICP criterion is sourced: JTS Traumatic Brain Injury Management in Prolonged Field Care, p.6, 'Suspect high ICP in any head injury patient with GCS score <=8 OR declining findings on neurologic examination.' Owner ruling (#98): unsigned draft, inert.

rows.condition: a basilar skull fracture, or its signs
rows.hold_text: The answer advised an NG tube, but a basilar skull fracture, or its signs, is recorded. A nasal tube is a recognised contraindication here. Use local protocol and medical control.
rows.extraction_notes: No corpus passage found (#98). The signs are listed in JTS Use of TBI WB Biomarkers after a Potentially Concussive Event, p.6: 'signs of a basilar skull fracture (e.g., raccoon eyes, Battle's sign, otorrhea)'. Owner ruling (#98): unsigned draft, inert; the owner will look for a source in NASEMSO or SMOG.

rows.hold_text: The answer advised a nasal airway, but mid-face trauma is recorded: JTS Airway Management in Prolonged Field Care (ID80) p.18 lists mid-face trauma as a contraindication to an NPA. Use local protocol and medical control.

sources.citation: JTS Clinical Practice Guideline — Airway Management in Prolonged Field Care, CPG ID80, 01 May 2020, p.18

rows.extraction_notes: ID80 p.18 (PDF p.18), item 5, verbatim: 'NPA should be used to assist with face mask ventilations (unless obvious contraindications such as mid-face trauma). OPA are also effective in obtunded patients or those who have received chemical sedation or neuromuscular blockade.' Owner ruling (#98): mid-face trauma only; basilar skull fracture needs its own source. SIGNED 2026-09-27: Andrew Azelton, after reading ID80 p.18.

rows.condition: burns, spinal cord injury or hyperkalaemia
rows.hold_text: The answer advised succinylcholine, but burns, spinal cord injury or hyperkalaemia is recorded: JTS Anesthesia for Trauma Patients (ID40) p.3 lists these as contraindications and names rocuronium for these cases.

sources.citation: JTS Clinical Practice Guideline — Anesthesia for Trauma Patients, CPG ID40, 05 Apr 2021, item 5, p.3

rows.extraction_notes: ID40 p.3 (PDF p.3), item 5, verbatim: 'Rocuronium is a non-depolarizing neuromuscular relaxant useful in cases where succinylcholine may be contraindicated (e.g., burns, spinal cord injury, hyperkalemia).' VERIFIED 2026-09-27: the ID40 passage is on printed page 3, which is also PDF page 3, so the citation 'p.3' stands. CORRECTED 2026-09-27: JTS Airway Management in Trauma (ID39, 28 Jan 2026) p.28 removed as a source. Read against the PDF (Airway_Management_in_Trauma_28_Jan_2026_ID39.pdf), p.28 doses succinylcholine (1.5 mg/kg IV/IO; 2 mg/kg under 5 years) but lists no contraindication, and no page of that edition lists burns, spinal cord injury or hyperkalaemia for it. Owner ruling (#100): cite ID40 p.3 alone; the signature stands. Owner rulings (#98): 'burns' with no timing qualifier; crush is a separate contract re-sign citing SMOG p.156; a stated potassium of 5.5 mmol/L or more counts as hyperkalaemia (owner ruling, not a citation). SIGNED 2026-09-27: Andrew Azelton, after reading ID40 p.3.
